meta.note: Values below are representative handbook/typical-batch figures (comparable to MMPDS, MatWeb, and standard aerospace materials references), not a specific mill certification. Real properties vary by heat treatment, batch, test temperature, and manufacturer -- verify against a datasheet before citing an exact number to a HAL panel. All values room-temperature unless otherwise noted.

items.garun_relevance: Reference material for the turboshaft engine's hot-section components (§5.4 propulsion chain) if a structural weight estimate is ever required beyond PS1's stated scope.
items.description: The most widely used aerospace superalloy overall; excellent strength retention up to ~650 C and good weldability relative to other superalloys, which is why it dominates turbine-disk and casing applications.

items.garun_relevance: Relevant if modeling the exhaust/tailpipe section of the series-hybrid engine, which sees both high temperature and corrosive combustion products.
items.description: Chosen over Inconel 718 where corrosion/oxidation resistance at very high temperature matters more than peak strength; lower strength but far higher elongation and oxidation resistance.

items.garun_relevance: Higher-temperature alternative to Inconel 718 if the BSFC map (§5.6) implies sustained high-power operation near the engine's rated limit.
items.description: Historically used in high-performance jet engines and rocket structures (e.g. X-15) where 718's ~700 C ceiling isn't sufficient.

items.garun_relevance: The combustor-can-class material if a future GARUN iteration models internal engine geometry rather than treating the engine as a black-box BSFC lookup.
items.description: Prioritizes oxidation/fatigue resistance at very high temperature over strength -- used where components see the most direct flame exposure in a gas turbine.

items.garun_relevance: Classic small-turboshaft turbine-blade material, directly relevant to the 60 kW-class engine assumed in your blueprint's propulsion sizing.
items.description: One of the earliest widely-used nickel superalloys; still common in small/medium turboshaft turbine sections due to good creep resistance and manufacturability.
